notes: Origin: one of the twelve root cases of the retired obstructed corpus.
Old title: "Joint-loop equivalence: red_blue linear vs non-linear (naive)" (kind: equiv-pair; algorithm: naive).

Prior classification and evidence in the retired corpus: valid, by a hand-written Lean kernel certificate (direct Lean kernel proof characterizing Ta/Tb/Tc/Td as the BB/BR/RB/RR alternating red/blue path relations, proving fixed-point completeness of the linear equations, reducing every nonlinear fixed point to the same closure, and deriving equality of all four outputs at joint-loop termination; no external FOL assumptions). The retired corpus records this case among the twelve valid, conjecturally FO-obstructed cases (no archived Vampire refutation for this particular case). That kernel certificate is not carried into this corpus; the classification here is unknown until re-certified.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example0134.lean` states the two Datalog programs written for this case, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots to the auxiliary input names `X_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` and `inputPost` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence. The two programs are independent, so the preprocessor merges them into the flag-free guarded parallel form.

The retired file's loop iterated destructively, carrying a second copy `SaX` of each relation and stepping the immediate-consequence operator from the empty relation; the compiled form accumulates, `T := T ∪ T_P(T)`, and reaches the same least fixpoint. The retired postcondition `(TaX = TaY) ∧ ((TbX = TbY) ∧ ((TcX = TcY) ∧ (TdX = TdY)))` was stated over those previous-round copies, which equal the fixpoints at loop exit; the same equalities are stated here over the compiled output relations, so the triple says the same thing. The schema loses the copies `SaX`, `SbX`, `ScX`, `SdX`, `SaY`, `SbY`, `ScY`, `SdY` and gains the compiler's snapshots `TaX_aux`, `TbX_aux`, `TcX_aux`, `TdX_aux`, `TaY_aux`, `TbY_aux`, `TcY_aux`, `TdY_aux`. The precondition `true` is unchanged, and the expected verdict stays valid.
title: Red/blue alternating paths: linear versus non-linear program (two compiled loops)
explanation: The command runs two independently compiled Datalog programs in sequence, each computing the four families of colour-alternating walks in a red/blue-edged graph (walks that start and end blue, start blue end red, start red end blue, and start and end red) — one program linear, the other non-linear — merged by the preprocessor into a single verified loop. The postcondition states that all four output relations from the linear program equal the corresponding relations from the non-linear program, so the Hoare triple is an equivalence claim between two implementations of colour-alternating reachability, both converging to the same least fixpoints.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true, imposing no constraint on the input relations.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts that all four linear-program outputs equal the corresponding non-linear-program outputs: TaX=TaY, TbX=TbY, TcX=TcY, and TdX=TdY.

datalog.label: programX — Colour-alternating walks, linearly.
datalog.text:
TaX(x1, y1) :- B(x1, y1).
TaX(x1, y1) :- B(x1, z1), TcX(z1, y1).
TbX(x1, y1) :- TaX(x1, z1), R(z1, y1).
TcX(x1, y1) :- TdX(x1, z1), B(z1, y1).
TdX(x1, y1) :- R(x1, y1).
TdX(x1, y1) :- R(x1, z1), TbX(z1, y1).
datalog.provenance: fidelity module (kernel-checked: the compiled sides of the command are this program's naive compilation)

datalog.label: programY — Colour-alternating walks, non-linearly.
datalog.text:
TaY(x1, y1) :- B(x1, y1).
TaY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TcY(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- B(x1, z1), R(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TdY(z1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- R(x1, z1), B(z1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- TdY(x1, z1), TaY(z1, y1).
TdY(x1, y1) :- R(x1, y1).
TdY(x1, y1) :- TdY(x1, z1), TbY(z1, y1).
